rule: fb2 media-register posts (Sion, 17:52 BST 23 Oct 2026: "Publish all"): every public register item dated 1995 or later, from /home/user/tab/work/media-register/register.json via work/chronology/fb_items.json. Post = 1–2 sentence neutral summary, the source's own title as the quote, hashtags; dated to publication (year-only and month-only items show only the year or month, the site's convention); Source = the item's URL, its Internet Archive copy when one exists, and the media register page. Embeddable YouTube items play on a tap through youtube-nocookie; unavailable ones are link only. Never in the shorts unless they carry a photo, mp4 or hyperframe.

posts.text: The Daily Express carried a classified advertisement for Ideal Homes four-bedroom houses at Church View Close, Llandough, built on the former farm land.
posts.key: LLANDOUGH, Church View Close. 4 bed houses
src: The report: Daily Express 3 Feb 1995 p.55

posts.text: The Echo’s property column reported that a third of the Church View Close development at Llandough had sold.
posts.key: LLANDOUGH IDEAL: A third of the Church View Close development has been sold
src: The report: South Wales Echo 16 Mar 1995 p.83

posts.text: An Echo property feature covered the Ideal Homes development beside St Dochdwy’s Church, and how a local Sunday School pupil chose the name Church View Close.
posts.key: Jenny has the right idea
src: The report: South Wales Echo 5 Oct 1995 p.79

posts.text: The London Gazette published the members’ voluntary winding-up of Western Ground Rents Ltd (company no. 342092), with a notice to creditors and, in April 1997, notice of the final meetings.
posts.key: London Gazette, 3 July 1996 (Issue 54455, p. 8982): Western Ground Rents Ltd (no. 342092) placed in members’ voluntary l

posts.text: An Echo property feature covered Churchview Close beside St Dochdwy’s, Llandough: building began in 1994, Persimmon bought Ideal Homes in early 1996, and the last house there sold by that September.
posts.key: Ideal Homes' select Churchview Close development in Llandough (property feature)
src: The report: South Wales Echo, Thursday 26 September 1996, p.79 (Property)

posts.text: Medieval Archaeology published the full report on the 1994 excavation at Llandough: 1,026 burials from an early-medieval monastic cemetery beside the Roman villa. The excavating unit’s free copy is linked below.
posts.key: An Early-medieval Monastic Cemetery at Llandough, Glamorgan: Excavations in 1994

posts.text: A companion paper in Medieval Archaeology set the Llandough excavation in context, from the Roman villa to the early-medieval monastery.
posts.key: From Villa to Monastery: Llandough in Context

posts.text: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales blogged about one skeleton, burial 631, from the 1994 Llandough excavation.
posts.key: The suffering of burial 631
src: The post: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales

posts.text: A Hong Kong land-law blog discussed the 1987 Court of Appeal decision on how a unilateral licence can stop time running for adverse possession.
posts.key: Unilateral licence can stop time running for adverse possession
src: The post: HK Land Law blog

posts.text: A blog post set out the historical, archaeological and family record of Great House Farm.
posts.key: The Great House Farm Story

posts.text: Coflein, the national record of the RCAHMW, holds a site record for the early-medieval cemetery excavated at Llandough in 1994 (project archive CA017).
posts.key: Coflein NPRN 802090: Llandough early medieval cemetery

posts.text: An open-access journal article on early-medieval diet in western Britain includes isotope data from the Llandough cemetery.
posts.key: A multi-isotope investigation of diet and subsistence amongst island and mainland populations from early medieval western Britain

posts.key: Great House Farm, Llandough. (entrance gate)

posts.key: The early medieval monument at Llandough, near Cardiff

posts.key: 1988 Dispossession of Great House Farm, Llandough from the Williams/ Buckler Family

posts.key: Great House Farm, Llandough (ATISN 27021)

posts.text: A local-history blog described the Irbic cross in St Dochdwy’s churchyard: a Sutton-stone pillar-cross of the 10th–11th century with its IRBICI inscription.
posts.key: sconzani: Llandough : the Irbic cross

posts.text: A local-history blog traced St Dochdwy’s Church: the earlier church moved stone by stone to Leckwith, and the present church consecrated in 1866.
posts.key: sconzani: Llandough : St Dochdwy's Church

posts.text: The Heneb Historic Environment Record for Llandough Roman Villa: Iron Age farmstead, a two-phase Roman villa, early-medieval burials and a medieval grange, linked to the Great House Farm cemetery record.
posts.key: Heneb Historic Environment Record: GGAT00768s

posts.text: The Vale of Glamorgan County Treasures survey recorded the locally important buildings of Llandough near Penarth.
posts.key: Llandough County Treasures Report

posts.text: The family’s Instagram carousel set four plans of the farm side by side, from the 1824 Bute estate survey to the May 1939 agreement plan.
posts.key: One Welsh farm on four maps, 1824–1939. Swipe through.

posts.text: The family’s Instagram reel explained the 1841 tithe apportionment: the Marquess of Bute as landowner, John Williams as occupier, 36 parcels of about 119 acres.
posts.key: How to read an 1841 farm record in 3 steps.

posts.text: A rail-heritage channel visited the disused Penarth Dock station and the short-lived halt at Llandough; viewers’ comments recall the Llandough sidings still busy in 1963.
posts.key: Penarth Dock, the staion and the strange halt at Llandough

posts.text: The Parish of Penarth & Llandough introduced the parish, St Dochdwy’s included, in a short video.
posts.key: About the Parish of Penarth & Llandough

posts.text: A local councillor’s video set out proposals for 130 homes at the bottom of Llandough Hill and announced a public online meeting.
posts.key: Llandough Hill development

posts.text: The family’s Instagram carousel listed six kinds of record behind the farm’s story, from the 1881 census to the 1987 law report.
posts.key: What's in the archive? 6 kinds of record behind one Welsh farm's story, 1881 to 1992. Swipe through.

posts.text: Penarth Nub News ran a book excerpt on Roman South Wales, describing the Llandough villa and its bath block, excavated in 1979 ahead of development.
posts.key: 'Romans in South Wales' - An excerpt from Karl-James Langford's new book

posts.text: The family shared a video in the public Vale of Glamorgan HUB group, linking the dartboard timeline of the case.
posts.key: Vale of Glamorgan HUB: family video post linking the dartboard timeline

posts.text: The Research Framework for the Archaeology of Wales cites the 1994 Cotswold Archaeological Trust preliminary report on the excavations at Great House Farm, Llandough.
posts.key: EARLY MEDIEVAL WALES (research framework bibliography/review)

posts.text: The Penarth Times reported residents’ concern over a proposal for about 136 homes on land south of Llandough Hill and Penarth Road.
posts.key: Concern over proposed big housing development near Penarth

posts.text: The Penarth Times reported that the Vale of Glamorgan Council planning committee granted outline permission for 133 homes south of Llandough Hill.
posts.key: Plans for 133 new homes in Llandough approved

posts.text: A reader’s letter in the Penarth Times recalled the monastery at Llandough and the gift of Llandough lands to Tewkesbury Abbey around 1106.
posts.key: History of St Mary’s

posts.text: Current Archaeology carried an article by the excavation directors on Llandough church and the 1994 cemetery excavation.
posts.key: Llandough (Current Archaeology 146, pp. 73-77)
